evidence.quote: Putting it all together, my reading of the evidence is that we are seeing a fairly significant pattern of reaching-for-yield behavior emerging in corporate credit.
I can imagine situations where it might make sense to enlist monetary policy tools in the pursuit of financial stability.
For example, a prolonged period of low interest rates, of the sort we are experiencing today, can create incentives for agents to take on greater duration or credit risks
Waiting for decisive proof of market overheating may amount to an implicit policy of inaction on this dimension.
not as a currently actionable policy proposal, but as an extended hypothetical meant to give some tangible substance to a broader theme.

parsed.rationale: The speech focuses on financial stability, highlighting reaching-for-yield risks from prolonged low rates and arguing monetary policy should not be fully decoupled from financial stability. That implies a mild hawkish lean, though it makes no direct call on near-term rates and frames the balance-sheet idea as hypothetical.
